title: Alternating Groups II
summary: Given an array of integers representing the colors of tiles in a circle, where 0 is red and 1 is blue, count the number of k-tile groups where each tile alternates in color with its neighbors, considering the first and last tiles as adjacent.
statement: Given an array of integers representing the colors of tiles in a circle, where 0 is red and 1 is blue, count the number of k-tile groups where each tile alternates in color with its neighbors, considering the first and last tiles as adjacent.
constraints: colors is a circular binary array and 2≤k≤len(colors).
A length-k group begins at any tile and follows clockwise with wraparound.
Count starts for which every adjacent pair within the group has different colors.
reference_solution:
def circular_alternating_groups(colors,k):
    n=len(colors);run=1;answer=0
    for index in range(1,n+k-1):
        if colors[index%n]!=colors[(index-1)%n]:run+=1
        else:run=1
        if index>=k-1 and run>=k:answer+=1
    return answer

A length-k window alternates exactly when the alternating suffix ending there has length at least k; the scanned endpoints correspond one-to-one with circular starts.

tests.explanation: Starts zero, one, and two produce alternating triples; the two groups crossing the equal circular boundary do not.
The full four-tile circle alternates along the three edges inside each linearized group, so all four starts count.
